texts: good. the arrival, Coraline Ash as the one arriving, Aelmere as the place, and both "late summer" and Year 1 as time information are all carried. Aelmere is left untyped, which is correct - the sentence never says what kind of place it is.

good. the two-day gap is stored as a measured before-relation between this arrival and the equinox, and the arrival is correctly treated as the same event as in the first sentence rather than a second one; the equinox is given only its class and the ordering, with no occurrence of its own asserted.

good. the journey, the market boat as the means of travel, the village as the origin, and "down the coast" kept on the village are all carried faithfully. Note that "came" is recorded as its own event, separate from the "arrived" of the first two sentences - the translator never merges two different verbs, so if this is meant to be the same journey, use the same verb.

mixed: the meeting comes out as one event with both people as participants, which is the reading you want, but a bare transitive "met" has no rule behind that shape - the ordinary object test would instead make Coraline Ash a plain object of the meeting, so the encoding can flip between runs and stop matching questions. Rewrite as "Old Vesh and Coraline Ash met at the harbor." - a joint subject with a reciprocal verb is the covered wording for exactly these atoms; "Old Vesh met with Coraline Ash at the harbor." also works if you want to keep Old Vesh in subject position.

good. Old Vesh is the walker, Coraline Ash is recorded as a companion in the walk rather than as a means, the destination is carried, and the Watch is treated as a definite common-noun referent with no name invented for it.
